candidates.title: Draft iOS app store listing improvements

demandEvidence.chore: Help iOS apps get more users through app store optimization.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I built this ASO tool to help you get more users for your iOS apps

ease.reason: A student could draft listing suggestions from sample app text, but no implementation reference supports keyword or listing analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent iOS developers may pay for listing help; this maker title establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can draft edits from operator supplied listing text, but useful inputs, evaluation criteria and results are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed text-to-suggestion loop is bounded, but no automated analysis is documented and a person must assess and approve edits.

evidence.reason: The post title states an ASO tool aims to help iOS apps gain users, but gives no task detail, frequency, results or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed the concrete but broad app store optimization task. A small listing suggestion experiment is imaginable, but the single maker title lacks workflow detail, implementation support and verified customer demand; the honest ratings are below threshold.

rejected.title: Draft iOS app store listing improvements
rejected.reason: Below threshold: the post only broadly says its ASO tool helps iOS apps gain users. It gives no bounded listing task, workflow, results or buyer evidence, and no supplied implementation reference supports the proposed automation.
